body.statement:
For every \(n\) and every feasible \(	heta\in\Theta_n\) with \(\Delta_n(	heta)>0\), use the null-supported moment-matching handle with cell amplitudes drawn from \(
u_	heta\) to construct priors \(\Pi_{0,	heta}\) and \(\Pi_{1,	heta}\) supported respectively on \(\mathcal H_0\) and \(\mathcal H_1(c_{\mathrm{lb}}\Delta_n(	heta))\), where \(c_{\mathrm{lb}}>0\) depends only on \(\alpha, eta,\gamma,d,L\). Every null component must satisfy \(	au\equiv c_{\mathrm{null}}\) for one \(c_{\mathrm{null}}\in I\), and every component must obey the unchanged binary margins, exact uniform design, and all three Hölder restrictions, verified using the actual support radius \(b_
u(	heta)\). Prove that the induced fixed-sample laws satisfy \[\operatorname{TV}(\Pi_{0,	heta}P^{\otimes n},\Pi_{1,	heta}P^{\otimes n})\le V_n(	heta).\] In the case \(d=\gamma=1\) and \(\alpha= eta=1/10\), verify directly that the two-observation shared-cell likelihood coefficient equals \(4(2A_i-1)(2A_k-1)B_j(X_i)B_j(X_k)\{q_e^2-\mathbb E_{
u_	heta}Z^2\}=0\), and derive the order-three, order-four, and tail contributions from this same \(
u_	heta\). Conclude parameterwise, without invoking an unknown target rate, that \(ho_n^*\ge c_{\mathrm{lb}}r_{\mathrm{mix}}(n)\).
body.justification: This parameterwise construction makes the lower optimization independently checkable and forces the rough-case repeated-observation coefficient and every higher-order remainder to come from one realizable bounded atomic law.
body.gap: KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024 uses localized fuzzy hypotheses with a nonuniform design support, and NeykovBalakrishnanWasserman2021 does not preserve a constant CATE in each null draw.
body.consumer: The converse prevents applied power claims from being benchmarked against an oracle or an easier null experiment.
